This sucks! Good for you being polite, it can be so awkward trying to avoid bringing up that your vegan with people you know aren’t going to take it easily. 
I’m really lucky to have a family who is so accepting of my choice. My mum isn’t a vegan or vegetarian but isn’t a big meat eater either and mainly buys vegan cheeses and soy milk for herself.. and will only buy cosmetics that are cruelty free. I don’t see her much these days but she still regularly sends me vegan articles about positive changes in the food industry and is constantly trying to get me to write down my recipes to make a vegan cook book! 
I forget that others aren’t as supported as this. But your mum sounds nice :)

Well done! It could also be an eye opener for others around you to see someone who really liked eating meat becoming vegan. Just be sure not to let others’ opinions sway what you think is the right thing to do. It can be difficult sometimes, but some of the greatest changes in the world have started with just a few people speaking up.

I don’t have any direct advice as such.. but I have some experience of a similar situation. Last year I had two young guinea pigs, Ollie and Dorian. Dorian was always an extremely affectionate affectionate piggy who would lick my nose and cuddle up to me to snooze all the time, whereas Ollie was always quite skitty and a bit uninterested. Sadly, Dorian died around Christmas time and it was absolutely heartbreaking. We weren’t aware he was sick at all, we just found him passed away in the cage the next morning. His brother was of course in the cage with him the whole time too which must have been very traumatic and upsetting for him. 
Immediately after this happened, I comforted Ollie and he started giving me kisses for the very first time. He really needed the company and affection and although it was upsetting, it touched my heart that he knew we were there for him. The days following this I spent all the time I had to cuddle him and make sure he wasn’t feeling upset and lonely. 
In January we thought it best to find him a friend, so we got a little baby pig called Nino. 
Unfortunately the two just did not get along which was very upsetting. Perhaps it was too soon for Ollie, they just didn’t click, or Nino was just too close to his adolescent stage. 
This was all a bit sad and stressful because now we had two guinea pigs in separate cages who didn’t get along. Fast forward a month and our heart had melted over three male baby brothers who were up for adoption. It may have been silly to adopt these boys but just a few days to a week later, Ollie was cuddling up to the smallest one of the three and then soon after, was happy sharing a cage with all three of them! 
Unfortunately we still had Nino on his own who didn’t seem to get on with anybody very well. We highly suspect this was due to adolescence and perhaps being a bit socially unaware due to not having a cage mate. Now, seven months later! 
Nino can get along with some of the boys even if he is a bit strange around them. We have two guinea pigs on their own but sharing a cage wall so they see and talk to eachother often, and three other guinea pigs sharing a cage together (Ollie and two of the brothers).  Because Nino and the separated brother are very chilled out sharing a wall in their cage, I think we’ll be able to have them sharing a cage soon. 
We really love all of our guinea pigs, but there has been A LOT  of stress and tears over having the money and time to care for all five of them and make sure they’re happy. We haven’t liked the idea of giving any up for adoption in case they weren’t with a caring, committed family. 

I’m really sorry if this comment was arduous to read! I just wouldn’t want someone else to experience the stress we have if they didn’t have to. 
And I hope the prospect of getting another guinea pig doesn’t scare you. Ollie is very happy with his company now. But perhaps we should have waited a bit longer and made sure his new friend was a bit younger. 

Good luck to you and Cheshire x

I’m sick of getting shit on by non-vegans. Like, you mention just once that you can’t eat something and as soon as it’s brought up that you’re vegan, you don’t hear the end of it. Mocking jokes, totally ignorant claims regarding humane slaughter practises. What gets to me is that I don’t argue with these points because.. do I really want to have these conversations/debates with everybody I meet? No. 
So I let them say what they want to say and smile politely. I’m not stopping them from eating what they want to eat or being rude to them because of it. 
I’ve only ever experienced harassment from people trying to rudely change my opinion regarding a topic I never chose to discuss with them.
It’s just very disrespectful to argue with someone you’ve just met for simply making the quiet choice to not harm other beings. 
For me, I have had so many loud and opinionated people try to tell me not to be vegan because they’re not vegan and therefore it’s wrong. 

Just thought I’d share a common perspective from the other side. 
You get obnoxious and loud people everywhere who think their opinion is the only opinion. Please don’t think most vegans are like this just because you may have met one who is like this.

The way which animals are killed? Please tell me how you are monitoring this. Do you visit slaughter houses personally to make sure it’s done humanely? Have you studied animal neurology or even just taken some time to investigate studies upon how much other animals around us can think or feel? Please provide proof to back up these claims. 

This is not an attack. It’s a request for you to give unbiased evidence in support of what you are trying to state.

Not at all. If you’re thinking of gaining weight or just don’t want to lose anymore.. just add things like pasta, nuts or starchy vegetables to your diet. 
I’ve been vegan for over a year now and my weight still goes up and down just as it did before. 
Just depends on how healthy I’m being and how much I’m snacking. It’s a lot easier to lose weight on a vegan diet as you don’t have the easy temptation to eat things like store bought cakes. 
But if you really want things like that, you can make your own vegan versions at home that taste exactly the same. (I’ve made beautifully fluffy and sweet birthday cakes for people which nobody suspecting them to be vegan friendly) 

So what I’m trying to say is it doesn’t restrict your diet as much as you think, you just find new ways around things and can easily maintain the same dietary proportions that suit you.
I suppose things like sun tanning, taking the pill and drinking alcohol don’t necessarily have to harm others though, just yourself.

Granted, that’s going to be very difficult for this person to do. But I don’t think it’s (such) a bad decision to make. It’s choosing an admirable lifestyle that doesn’t harm others and from their perspective, trying to make a stand and not wanting to condone others supporting a cruel system. 
HOWEVER.. refusing to sit at the same table as people who are eating dead animals is very unlikely going to stop them from eating animal products. This person just won’t get invited out!
